content.thinking:
I'm putting the postmortem together now. The flag was switched on at 10:10:31 by an admin, and the logs show a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py from 10:10 to 10:16 while the flag was on. The account page's error rate peaked around 10:13, and the flag was turned back off at T18.

I'm working through the causal chain now: the account page requests failed because the spend-summary code raised a ZeroDivisionError once the monthly-spend flag was switched on. I'm also checking whether any deploy could account for it, and so far none turned up in the window.

I'm checking which causes are ruled out: no deploy turned up in the window read, and the flag being off earlier coincided with a healthy service. I'll keep the revert out of the step that names the change, since it's confirmation rather than elimination. The mechanism is that with the flag on, the spend-summary path divides by this month's purchase count, which is zero for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month.

I'm framing the root cause now: turning the monthly-spend flag on sends account-page rendering through a per-item average that divides by this month's purchase count, which fails with a ZeroDivisionError for shoppers who have past purchases but none this month. The mechanism rests on that reading of the code, since the logs show the error at line 47 but not why the divisor is zero.

I'm drafting the cause in plain words now: switching on the monthly spend summary made account pages fail with a division by zero, likely for shoppers who had bought before but hadn't yet bought this month. I'm also noting that the faulty code is still there, so turning the flag back on before a fix could bring the same failures back.

I'm listing the contributing factors now: the flag went from off to fully on within a minute with no staged rollout or health gate visible, and no test in the record covers the flagged-on path for a shopper with no purchases this month, so the fault wasn't caught before it reached production.

I'm listing the contributing factors: the flag went from off to fully on within a minute with no staged rollout or health gate visible, and no test in the record covers the flagged-on path for a shopper with no purchases this month. Nobody was paged either, since the alert linked no on-call incident, which I'll treat as a separate finding.

I'm weighing whether the alert's five-minute wait counts as a contributing factor, since a faster alert might have shortened the incident, but I don't have enough to claim that with confidence. I'll look for a more concrete gap around how the flag change itself is watched.

I'm settling the action items now: staged rollouts with an error-rate check that can halt and reverse a flag change, a CI requirement that every flag's on-path is tested before it can go live in production, and linking the high-error-rate alert to an on-call rotation so someone gets paged.

I'm checking the timeline notes now: the onset at 10:10 is tied to the flag change, the revert came at T18, the watch confirmed recovery at T21, and a draft fix PR was proposed at T23. The lapse I'm noting is that nobody got paged.

I'm working out how to describe the timing in the report without restating figures I've already placed, and checking that each reference to the logs and the flag change points at the right source.

I'm checking the ruled-out causes now: no deploy showed up in the change records from before the onset, and the only flag change anyone else made in that hour was a single one, so other flag toggles are out as well. I'm also noting that the account-page failures are the symptom to describe.

action_items.item: Roll out feature flag changes on io-shop in stages, with an error-rate check that stops the rollout and turns the flag back off when errors rise.
Require tests that exercise a flag's on path to pass in CI before that flag can be switched on in production.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors appear in the logs only from {G5309.3}, and no such error was logged before then.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or release: none came back from the day of production changes read before the onset.
Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read.

causal_chain.step: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on by admin at {P1.1}. Before that it was evaluated off and account pages rendered normally. Evaluations were split between off and on at {G971b.6} and were all on through {Gce95.4}.
With the flag on, account page requests reached a monthly per-item spend calculation that divides by zero for shoppers with no purchases this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary made the account page fail with a division by zero, likely for shoppers who had bought before but not yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag change reached all account page traffic straight away. Evaluations were split for one minute and all on from the next. No staged rollout or health check that would hold back or undo a flag change was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout gated on the error rate would have kept the failures to a small share of shoppers and stopped the change before it reached everyone.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test of the flag-on path for a shopper with past purchases but none this month was seen before the flag was switched on. Code-Fix says the cases it adds would raise against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been caught before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent tied the onset to the monthly-spend-feature flag change and the ZeroDivisionError log lines, and formed C1.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature back off. The change can be put back.
The Mitigation Agent watched the service, found it no longer at the incident's level and judged the action confirmed.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #570 for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's spend by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month` and does not handle an empty list. So for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, it raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns that error into a failed page.
input.still_at_risk: Switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place could make account pages fail again in the same way.
